transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

I guess... the main reason I came in is that I don’t really care about the things I used to care about, and it’s been bothering me. Like, I used to feel like myself when I went to dance class, or when I’d go hiking, or even just try out some new recipe because I saw it online and thought it looked fun. And game night too—normally that was something I looked forward to, something easy and familiar.

But lately all of that just feels like chores I keep putting off. Like they’re sitting there waiting for me, and I know they used to matter, but I can’t seem to feel that same pull toward them. It’s not even that I hate them now, exactly. It’s more like I look at them and think, “I should want to do this,” and then I just... don’t. That’s why I figured I should probably talk to someone, because those were the things that made me feel like me.
Has this feeling of not caring about things you used to enjoy been happening most days, and does it last throughout the day?

Yeah... I mean, it’s not like every single second of every day I’m actively thinking, “I don’t care,” but it’s there most days, definitely. It kind of follows me around in the background.

Like with dance class, hiking, trying a new recipe, even game night—those were things that used to make me feel like myself. Now they just sort of sit there in my mind like chores I keep putting off. I’ll think, “I should go,” or “I should make plans,” and then the whole day can pass and I still haven’t done it, or I’ll do it and feel kind of disconnected from it. So yes, most days, and it can last through a lot of the day, just this flat feeling toward things I used to actually want.
Do you feel down or depressed most of the day, or is your mood more neutral or flat?

It’s… I don’t know if I’d call it “depressed” exactly, not all the time. It’s more like this low, sour feeling that sits underneath everything most days. Like even if nothing bad is happening in that moment, I still feel tense or scared in this quiet way, and guilty too, like I’ve done something wrong or I should have handled things differently.

So my mood isn’t exactly neutral. Flat, maybe sometimes, but there’s usually something unpleasant under it. It’s like I’m carrying this background fear and guilt around with me, and it kind of colors the whole day even when I’m just doing normal things.
Have you noticed a change in your energy levels lately, like feeling more tired than usual or finding it harder to get through the day?

I’m not really sure, honestly. I haven’t been tracking my energy in a clear way, like “I’m exhausted” or anything like that. Some days it feels harder to get moving, but I don’t know if that’s energy exactly or just... not wanting to do things, if that makes sense.

Like, I can still get through basic parts of the day most of the time. It’s more that I’ll sit there thinking about doing something and it feels like there’s this wall in front of it. But I haven’t noticed some big physical tiredness where I’m sleeping all day or can’t stand up or anything. It’s kind of hard for me to separate being tired from just feeling unmotivated and weighed down.
Have you found it harder to focus on things lately, like following a conversation, reading, or making decisions?

Yeah, I think so. It’s not like I can’t understand things, exactly, but I get stuck in a way I didn’t used to.

Like, I’ve been trying to work on these catering forms and a Chamber application, and I’ll read the same line over and over again, and it’s like my eyes are moving but nothing is really landing. Then I start second-guessing tiny things, like what price to put down, or which email I should answer first, and suddenly I’ve spent way too long doing almost nothing.

It’s frustrating because the tasks aren’t even that complicated. They’re normal little decisions, but my brain kind of locks up on them. Then I feel like I need to step away, but when I come back, I’m still stuck in the same spot.
Can you think of a time recently when you felt any real enjoyment or interest in doing something, even for a short moment, or has that completely stopped?

I wouldn’t say it’s completely stopped, but… it’s close enough that it scares me a little. I came in partly because I barely care about the things that used to make me feel like myself. Like dance class — I used to look forward to it, even if I was nervous or tired, because once I got there I’d feel like, okay, this is me, I’m in my body, I’m doing something good. Now I’ll see the class on my calendar and it just feels like another obligation I’m avoiding.

Same with hiking. I used to like planning a trail, packing snacks, even just being outside and having a reason to move. Now I think about it and it feels like so much effort before I’ve even put my shoes on. Trying new recipes used to be fun too, like I could spend time looking up ingredients or imagining how something would turn out, and now it’s like… why bother, I’ll just make whatever is easiest.

Even game night, which should be simple and fun, feels like a chore I keep putting off. I don’t get that little spark of interest much anymore. Sometimes I’ll have a tiny moment where I think, maybe this would be nice, but it fades really fast and then I’m back to not caring enough to actually do it.
Have these feelings started to interfere with your ability to function in your daily life, like at work, in relationships, or with taking care of yourself?

Yeah… it has. I think that’s actually the part that made me finally admit I probably needed to talk to someone, because it’s not just “I feel off” anymore. It’s showing up in real things I’m supposed to be doing.

Like with the Chamber application, I’ve missed deadlines. Not because I didn’t care at all, or because it wasn’t important, but because every time I tried to sit down and deal with it, the paperwork felt like too much, and then I’d put it off, and then suddenly the deadline was gone. And with the catering stuff, I keep telling myself I’m going to get things moving again, make a plan, reach out to people, handle the jobs and the forms and all of that… but I don’t trust myself to keep up with it the way I used to. So I keep putting the whole thing on hold.

And socially, too. I see friends less. I don’t really make plans like I used to, and when people invite me to things, I’ll often think about whether it feels manageable or safe instead of whether it sounds fun. So my life feels like it’s gotten smaller, if that makes sense. Like I’m mostly staying inside this little circle of what feels okay, and anything outside of that feels like too much to deal with.
Has there been a time in the last two weeks when you felt absolutely no interest or pleasure in something you used to really enjoy, not even a little bit?

Yeah… there have been times like that. I don’t know if I’d say every single second, because sometimes I can still sort of imagine enjoying something, but when it comes down to actually doing it, it’s like there’s nothing there.

That’s part of why I came in. I barely care about the things that used to make me feel like myself. Dance class used to be one of those things where even if I was dragging myself there, once I got moving I’d remember why I loved it. But lately I’ll look at it on the calendar and feel absolutely nothing except, like, ugh, that’s another thing I should probably cancel.

Hiking is the same. Trying new recipes too, which sounds small, but that used to be a real thing for me — looking up ideas, getting ingredients, making something new. Now it all just sits there in my head like a chore I keep putting off. Even game night, which should be easy and fun, feels like something I’m supposed to want to do, but I don’t really feel that pull anymore. It’s just… flat.
Have you noticed any changes in your appetite or weight recently—like eating much less or much more than usual?

I’m not really sure, honestly. I haven’t been tracking my weight or anything, and I don’t think I’ve noticed some big obvious change, like my clothes suddenly fitting differently.

My eating has maybe been a little less consistent, but I don’t know if I’d call it “much less” or “much more.” Some days I just kind of eat whatever is easiest because I don’t want to think about it too much, and other days I realize later that I didn’t pay much attention to meals. But I can’t say I’ve had a clear appetite change that I’ve really noticed.
Have you felt unusually tired or noticed a significant loss of energy lately, even when you haven’t been physically active?

I don’t really know how to answer that clearly. I mean… I feel tired a lot, but I’m not sure if it’s the kind of tired you mean, like a real physical loss of energy, or if it’s more that I just feel worn down.

I haven’t noticed something like, “Oh, I can’t walk across the room,” or that my body is suddenly weak for no reason. It’s more that certain normal things feel like they take a lot more effort to start. But I don’t know if I’d call it significant, because I can still get up and do things when I absolutely have to. It just feels like I have to talk myself into it more than I used to.

So… maybe some tiredness, yeah, but I’m not sure I’ve noticed a major energy change in a way I could measure.
Have you noticed that your thoughts feel slower than usual, or that you're moving more slowly, like everything takes more effort or time?

I don’t think so… not in a way I’ve really noticed. Like, I don’t feel like I’m walking around in slow motion or that people are waiting on me because I’m moving so slowly.

Sometimes I do feel like it takes me longer to get started on things, but that feels more like I’m hesitating or getting stuck in my head, not like my body or my thoughts are actually slowed down. If you asked someone else watching me, I don’t know that they’d say I look slower.

My thoughts can feel kind of crowded or hard to organize sometimes, but not slow exactly. So I guess my answer is… I haven’t noticed a clear slowdown, no.
Have you experienced a complete loss of interest or pleasure in all activities, including things you used to enjoy or even things that used to bring you small moments of happiness?

Yeah… I mean, “complete loss” sounds so absolute, and I don’t know if I’d say literally every single thing is gone, like I can’t ever feel anything good for even a second. But honestly, that’s a big part of why I came in.

It’s like the things that used to make me feel like myself don’t really pull me in anymore. I used to love dance class—not just the exercise part, but the music and being around people and feeling like I was actually in my body for a while. And now it just sits there on the calendar like this chore I keep avoiding. Same with hiking. I used to look forward to getting out somewhere quiet, planning where to go, even packing snacks and all that. Now it feels like too much effort before I even start.

Even smaller things, like trying a new recipe, which used to be kind of fun for me… I’ll save one and think, “Maybe I’ll make that,” and then it just never happens. Game night too. That used to be easy happiness, you know? Laughing, being distracted, just feeling normal for a bit. Now I think about going and it feels like another obligation I have to get through.

So… not complete in the sense that I’m incapable of enjoying anything at all, maybe. But it’s definitely like I barely care about most of the things I used to enjoy, and that feels really unlike me.
Has this period of feeling this way—losing interest in things you used to enjoy and having this low mood—lasted for at least two weeks in a row?

Yes… definitely longer than two weeks. It’s been going on since the robbery at that festival job, which was about two years and three months ago now.

I mean, it hasn’t felt exactly the same every single day that whole time—some days I can sort of push through better than others—but the loss of interest and that low, heavy feeling have been there pretty consistently since then. It’s not like it was just a bad couple of weeks and then I bounced back. It feels like it started after that happened and just… never really went back to how I was before.
Have you noticed yourself losing a significant amount of weight recently, even when you weren’t trying to?

Um… no, I don’t think so. I haven’t been trying to lose weight, and I also haven’t noticed my clothes suddenly fitting differently or anything like that. I don’t weigh myself all the time, so I guess I can’t say with total precision, like “exactly no pounds,” but nothing has stood out to me as a significant weight loss.

If anything, it’s not something I’ve been tracking closely. But no, I haven’t had that experience where people are commenting on it or where I’m realizing I’ve dropped a lot without meaning to.
Have you noticed that you're moving more slowly than usual, or that your thoughts feel slowed down or more difficult to get going?

Yeah… more with my thoughts than, like, physically moving slow, I think. I don’t know if other people would look at me and say I’m moving in slow motion or anything, but in my head it definitely feels like things take way longer to start.

Like, if I’m trying to work on catering forms or an application for the Chamber, I’ll open it and just sit there. I read the same line over and over and it’s like the words aren’t turning into a decision. Then I get stuck on these tiny things that should not be that hard, like what price to put down, or which email I should answer first, and I can lose so much time just circling around it.

It’s frustrating because it’s not that I don’t understand what the form is asking. I do. It’s just like my brain won’t move from reading it to actually doing the next step. And then I start second-guessing every little choice, so even something simple feels like wading through mud.
Would you say that you’ve been feeling fatigued or that you’ve had a loss of energy nearly every day?

I’m not totally sure how to answer that one. I mean… I do have days where I feel worn out, but I don’t know that I’d say it’s nearly every single day in a clear way, or that it’s this separate thing where I’m just physically exhausted all the time.

Sometimes I think it’s more like I get drained from trying to get through the day, if that makes sense, but I haven’t really been tracking it. I don’t wake up every morning thinking, “I have no energy,” or anything that specific. It’s more mixed, I guess. Some days I can get going better than others, and some days everything feels like it takes more out of me.

So… I don’t know. I wouldn’t want to say yes if that means like a constant, nearly daily loss of energy, because I’m not sure that’s accurate.
Would you say that you’ve had trouble thinking clearly or concentrating nearly every day?

Yeah… I think so, at least with concentrating. It’s not like I can’t think at all, but it feels like my mind gets sticky, if that makes sense.

Like when I try to sit down and do catering forms or an application for the Chamber, I’ll read the same line over and over, and I know the words are there, but I’m not really taking them in. Then I get hung up on these small choices that should be simple, like what price to put down or which email I should answer first, and suddenly I’ve spent all this time just staring at it.

So, yes, I’d say trouble thinking clearly and concentrating has been happening a lot. I don’t know if I’ve counted it as “nearly every day,” but it comes up enough that it’s definitely affecting me.
Would you say that you’ve had trouble thinking clearly or concentrating nearly every day?

Yeah, I would say so. I know I kind of already said this, but that’s the main place I notice it—when I’m trying to sit down and do paperwork for catering, or something like that Chamber application.

I’ll look at a line on the form and read it, and then realize I didn’t actually absorb it, so I read it again. And then again. It’s not that the words are too hard or I don’t understand what they mean exactly, it’s more like my brain doesn’t move forward with it. Then I get stuck on some small decision, like what price I should put down, or whether I should answer one email before another, and it turns into this whole thing in my head.

It’s embarrassing, honestly, because those are normal little tasks. They shouldn’t take that much out of me. But I’ll just sit there circling around it, and by the time I realize how long I’ve been stuck, I feel even more frustrated. So yes, trouble concentrating and thinking clearly has definitely been happening a lot.
Would you say that you’ve completely lost interest or pleasure in almost all activities, to the point where very little, if anything, brings you satisfaction anymore?

Yeah… that’s actually a big part of why I came in. I don’t know if I’d say literally nothing brings me anything anymore, but it’s close enough that it scares me.

The things that used to make me feel like myself just… don’t pull me in now. Dance class used to be one of those things where even if I didn’t feel like going, once I was there I’d come out feeling lighter. Hiking too—getting outside, having a trail to focus on, that used to really help me feel grounded. And now I think about going and it just feels like another task I’m avoiding.

Even smaller stuff, like trying a new recipe, which I used to get really into, or game night… they all just kind of sit there in my mind like chores I keep putting off. It’s not that I hate them. It’s more like I barely care, and then I feel bad because I know I used to care. So, yeah, I’ve lost a lot of interest and pleasure in things that used to matter to me.

Like dance class — I used to look forward to it, even if I was nervous or tired, because once I got there I’d feel like, okay, this is me, I’m in my body, I’m doing something good. Now I’ll see the class on my calendar and it just feels like another obligation I’m avoiding.

Same with hiking. I used to like planning a trail, packing snacks, even just being outside and having a reason to move. Now I think about it and it feels like so much effort before I’ve even put my shoes on. Trying new recipes used to be fun too, like I could spend time looking up ingredients or imagining how something would turn out, and now it’s like… why bother, I’ll just make whatever is easiest.

patient.answer:
Yeah… it has. I think that’s actually the part that made me finally admit I probably needed to talk to someone, because it’s not just “I feel off” anymore. It’s showing up in real things I’m supposed to be doing.

Like with the Chamber application, I’ve missed deadlines. Not because I didn’t care at all, or because it wasn’t important, but because every time I tried to sit down and deal with it, the paperwork felt like too much, and then I’d put it off, and then suddenly the deadline was gone. And with the catering stuff, I keep telling myself I’m going to get things moving again, make a plan, reach out to people, handle the jobs and the forms and all of that… but I don’t trust myself to keep up with it the way I used to. So I keep putting the whole thing on hold.

And socially, too. I see friends less. I don’t really make plans like I used to, and when people invite me to things, I’ll often think about whether it feels manageable or safe instead of whether it sounds fun. So my life feels like it’s gotten smaller, if that makes sense. Like I’m mostly staying inside this little circle of what feels okay, and anything outside of that feels like too much to deal with.
